title: Coherent control of subradiant excitations in atomic rings
authors: Milena Djatchkova, Igor Lesanovsky, Beatriz Olmos
abstract: Collective excitations in ordered subwavelength atomic arrays can exhibit strongly suppressed radiative decay due to interference between light scattered by neighboring emitters. These so-called subradiant states make these systems a promising platform for storing and manipulating photonic excitations. The external geometry of the array, combined with dynamical control of the atomic dipole orientation, enables localized trapping and coherent transport of these subradiant excitations. Here, we theoretically demonstrate these capabilities in ring-shaped atomic arrays. Specifically, we show adiabatic transport of a localized excitation around a single ring, coherent transfer of a single excitation between two neighboring rings with geometry-controlled selectivity, and interaction-induced conditional phase shifts between two simultaneously trapped excitations in neighboring rings. The latter can be interpreted as effective controlled-phase operations between stored excitations. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of ordered atomic arrays as a platform for coherent photonic quantum information processing with dissipation-protected collective excitations.
summary: The authors theoretically demonstrate that ordered atomic rings can act as robust quantum memories and processors for photonic excitations. By controlling dipole orientation and inter-ring spacing, they achieve coherent transport and controlled interactions between stored subradiant light quanta. This establishes the platform's potential for fault-tolerant quantum information processing.
main_problem: The paper demonstrates how coherent control can be achieved for subradiant excitations trapped within ordered atomic rings.
main_result: They show that the system supports adiabatic transport around a ring, geometry-controlled transfer between neighboring rings, and interaction-induced conditional phase shifts, enabling photonic quantum information processing.
method: The analysis uses theoretical modeling based on the master equation and effective Hamiltonians derived for collective excitations in atomic arrays.
model_or_system: The system consists of ordered subwavelength atomic arrays, specifically ring-shaped structures containing two-level emitters. Dynamics are governed by coupling terms ($V_{\alpha eta}$) and dissipation ($\Gamma_{\alpha eta}$), analyzed within the single or two-excitation manifold.
key_observables: Collective excitation survival probability ($P_{	ext{sur}}$), single-excitation transfer probability ($P_{tr}$), and interaction-induced excess phase ($\Delta\phi$).
important_parameters: Interatomic separation ($r_{\alpha eta}$), dipole orientation ($	heta$), ring separation ($f$), and the requirement for subradiant protection.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system remains largely confined to the single-excitation manifold, and adiabatic evolution requires slow changes relative to energy gaps.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate excitation transport during dipole rotation (Fig. 1), controlled exchange dynamics between two rings based on geometry (Fig. 2), and the dependence of phase accumulation and fidelity on separation distance (Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing single-ring adiabatic transport, then demonstrating controllable inter-ring transfer using symmetric vs. shifted geometries, and finally analyzing two-excitation dynamics to realize controlled-phase quantum gates.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the use of solid-state or structured matter platforms (atomic arrays) for building scalable photonic quantum circuits by leveraging engineered collective decay suppression.
